Right, for my words of wisdom today I am actually going to read the man in the arena, which I've talked about as being one of my favorite quote. It was written by PRESIDENT Roosevelt. The reason that I like this, especially as we start our first term is because of a couple of reasons. One, we are coming off of an election, it was an election. Let's just leave it at that.

Over the next four years we are going to receive a lot of the back. Much of it will be constructive. In fact most would be constructive feedback from citizens, from one another, from staff, everyone that we really should try to listen to. Every once in a while you will get feedback from people just because they choose to want to be critical without having any answers.

When that happens, I always try to think of roosevelt's words, which were the man in the arena. I read this to myself whenever I need to. I want to share this. Often when I say something it is for the good of the county or whatever, but my colleagues, today this is just for you. It is not the critic who counts, not the man who points out how the strong man stumbles or whether a doer of deeds could have done them

better. The credit belongs to the man or in this case woman who was actually in the arena, whose face is marred by dust, sweat and blood. Who strives violently. Who comes up short again and again, because there is no effort without error and short-coming, but who strives to do the deeds. Who spends

himself on a worthy cause. Who the best nose triumph in high achievement. And who would worst, if he fails, at least fails while daring greatly so that his or her place shall never be with those cold and timid souls who either know victory or defeat. allegiance.
